what_its_for: Baloxavir marboxil is an antiviral medicine used to treat influenza (the flu) in people who have had flu symptoms for no more than 48 hours. It works by stopping the flu virus from making copies of itself inside your body. It may also be used to prevent the flu if you have been in close contact with someone who has it.
how_to_take: Take this medicine by mouth as a single dose, with or without food. Swallow the tablet whole. Do not crush, chew, or split the tablet. If you have trouble swallowing the tablet, talk to your pharmacist or doctor about your options. Take it as soon as possible after your flu symptoms start — it works best when taken within 48 hours of symptom onset.
dosing: For most adults and children weighing 40 kg (about 88 lbs) or more, the usual dose is 40 mg taken as a single dose. For people weighing 80 kg (about 176 lbs) or more, the dose is usually 80 mg as a single dose. Children between 20 kg and 40 kg typically receive 20 mg as a single dose. Because this is usually a one-time dose, there is no daily schedule to follow. Always take the exact dose your doctor or pharmacist tells you to take.
missed_dose: Because baloxavir marboxil is typically taken as just one single dose, a missed dose situation is uncommon. However, if you forget to take your dose and it has been more than 48 hours since your flu symptoms started, contact your doctor before taking it, as it may be less effective. If you are using it to prevent the flu after exposure, take your dose as soon as you remember unless your doctor tells you otherwise.
storage: Store baloxavir marboxil at room temperature, between 68°F and 77°F (20°C and 25°C). Keep it in its original packaging and away from moisture and heat. Do not store it in the bathroom. Keep all medicines out of reach of children and pets. If you have leftover or unused medicine, ask your pharmacist how to safely dispose of it.
what_to_avoid: Avoid taking dairy products, calcium-fortified foods or drinks, antacids that contain calcium, aluminum, or magnesium, or laxatives and supplements that contain iron or zinc at the same time as your dose, as these can reduce how well the medicine works. Try to separate these by at least 2 hours before or after taking baloxavir. Avoid contact with people who are sick or have a weakened immune system while you have the flu, as you may still be contagious. Do not take live flu vaccines (such as the nasal spray flu vaccine) while using this medicine without talking to your doctor first.
when_to_call_doctor: Call your doctor right away or seek emergency help if you experience: a severe allergic reaction such as hives, swelling of your face, lips, tongue, or throat, or trouble breathing; unusual changes in behavior or mood, confusion, hallucinations, or talking or acting strangely (this is more common in children); skin blistering, peeling, or a severe rash; or if your flu symptoms are getting much worse or are not improving after a few days. Also tell your doctor if you are pregnant, planning to become pregnant, or breastfeeding before taking this medicine.
when_it_works: Baloxavir marboxil starts working right away after you take it, but you may not feel better immediately. Most people begin to notice improvement in their flu symptoms within 1 to 2 days after taking the dose. It can shorten the duration of the flu by about 1 day compared to not taking any treatment. It works best when taken as early as possible — ideally within the first 48 hours of feeling sick.
special_populations: Children: This medicine can be used in children as young as 5 years old who weigh at least 20 kg (about 44 lbs). The dose is based on the child's weight. Elderly patients: No dose adjustment is typically needed for older adults, but they should use it with caution and inform their doctor of all other medicines they take. Pregnant or breastfeeding women: There is limited safety data available. Talk to your doctor about the risks and benefits before using this medicine if you are pregnant or breastfeeding. Kidney or liver problems: No dose adjustment is generally required for mild to moderate kidney or liver issues, but let your doctor know about any kidney or liver conditions you have.
